servicesPreview.title: My services
servicesPreview.intro: I help companies design modern, user-centered technology. My way of working is rooted in a user-centered approach: understanding people’s needs, frustrations and expectations to design experiences that are both simple and impactful.

aboutPreview.photoAlt: Portrait of Serigne Khalifa Ababacar Sy Nguirane, smiling, in a white shirt with arms crossed
aboutPreview.text: With a degree in computer science, I started out in development, with plenty of curiosity and little experience. Then came a moment of doubt: what should I specialize in? I looked at what truly defines me: I am organized, very attentive to detail, and I like to think before I act. Those traits naturally led me to front-end, where I quickly realized I was missing a real sense of usability. That is when I discovered Figma, and with it an immediate ease in building mockups. I trained, and realized that UX design is not just about drawing: it is about understanding user behavior to design products that genuinely serve them. Little by little, my interest widened from UX to product design, with a more holistic view of the product. Today, I have a clear direction, many projects behind me, and I am more ready than ever to go further.

example.title: A concrete example
example.text: It all starts with a sheet of paper and a pencil. These sketches lay down the essentials: where the user searches, how they pick a destination, how they talk with their assistant. Once the structure is validated, it becomes a clear interface: a simple search, destinations within thumb’s reach, and two ways to talk with the assistant, by message or by voice. Same journey, same logic, but designed to be understood at first glance.
example.stepsLabel: From problem to interface: persona, sketches, mockups
example.personaAlt: Persona Awa, smiling, phone in hand at a café terrace in Dakar. Problem: Awa wants to discover places and activities without spending much, but she lacks reliable information, prices are not transparent, and organizing transport outside Dakar is difficult, which discourages her. Hypothesis: if the app offers places sorted by budget, Awa will easily find affordable activities; if prices are clear with promotions/deals, Awa will be more motivated to go out.
example.sketchesAlt: Pencil sketches of two Samba app screens: the home screen with search, filters and a destination card, then the assistant chat screen (message or voice) with its history
example.screensAlt: Final Samba app mockups: the home screen “Choose your next destination” featuring Lac Rose, and the message or voice chat screen with Samba and its history

samba.title: Samba App
samba.summary: An artificial intelligence to transform local tourism
samba.coverAlt: Three screens of the Samba mobile app: discovering Senegal, diving into the culture and the Samba mascot

slides.s1: Cover: the Samba app and its mascot, Samba the lion, with the tools used (Figma, Notion, Google Forms, ChatGPT)
slides.s2: About the project: goal, Samba app project, UX/UI role, tourism field, year 2026, with photos of Senegal
slides.s3: User research: 64% of tourism is consumed by locals, 80% of tourists find a local guide important, 50% face non-transparent pricing and no guide
slides.s4: Personas: Awa, young local explorer; Léa, international tourist; Mamadou, diaspora traveler, with their goals, frustrations, motivations and behaviors
slides.s5: Problem statement: a problem and a hypothesis for each of the three personas
slides.s6: “How might we” ideation: HMW questions and solution ideas on sticky notes
slides.s7: Impact / effort matrix used to prioritize features
slides.s8: Six-panel storyboard: a young woman discovers the Samba Travel app and visits a site with Samba
slides.s9: User flow: from opening the app to the home screen, Samba AI (chat or voice), search, map and guide mode
slides.s10: Sitemap: splash screen, onboarding, login, home, map, Samba AI, search, profile and destination page
slides.s11: Value proposition: the Samba mascot and the quote “thanks to AI and our mascot, we make tourism more human”
slides.s12: Wireframes: sketches of the home and Samba chat screens
slides.s13: Prototype – onboarding: meeting Samba, choosing the type of experience and the budget
slides.s14: Prototype – home page: search bar with filters, quick filters by region, destination cards and navbar
slides.s15: Prototype – Samba AI: message or voice discussion and conversation history
slides.s16: Prototype – chat with Samba: sending a message and an automatic answer with place suggestions
slides.s17: Prototype – voice discussion: talking to Samba and getting a voice answer with suggestions
slides.s18: Prototype – map and places: interactive map of tourist sites and the Lac Rose detail page
slides.s19: Thank you: splash, welcome and login screens of the Samba app
